# Synthetic DOCX test corpus

This corpus contains only small, synthetic DOCX files for parser and future
fixer golden tests. The source fixtures are committed in `generated/`; tests
must never modify them. `DocxFixtureWorkspace` calculates the original SHA-256,
copies the chosen fixture to a unique operating-system temporary directory, and
checks the original SHA-256 again during disposal. Any operation that could
mutate a DOCX must use that temporary working copy.

## Privacy and sanitization rules

- Only wholly synthetic data is allowed.
- Never add a student's name, NIM, email address, address, signature, reviewer
  comment, revision history, or metadata from a real student.
- Never copy a real thesis and replace only its name.
- Keep each fixture as small as possible and give it one clear test purpose.
- Do not add author, company, user, custom-property, or revision metadata.
- Before committing, verify the manifest has `synthetic: true` and
  `containsPersonalData: false`, run `npm run check:secrets`, and run the
  fixture tests. Inspect the proposed text and metadata without printing a full
  document in test logs.

## Structure

- `manifest.json` is the machine-readable inventory and initial expected
  semantic properties.
- `generated/` contains the source DOCX fixtures generated by the Open
  XML SDK.
- `expectedDocumentProperties` in the manifest is the focused golden semantic
  result. Canonical parser projections omit text and are compared in memory.
- The temporary workspace is outside the repository under the operating-system
  temporary directory and is deleted after each test.

## Regeneration and tests

Run these commands from the repository root:

```powershell
npm run fixtures:generate
npm run fixtures:generate
npm run fixtures:check
dotnet test backend/PpkiSmartFormatter.slnx --no-build
```

The generator uses only the existing Open XML SDK. It does not use Word,
LibreOffice, Supabase, internet access, or `.env`. It overwrites only the nine
known generated fixture paths with the same semantic structure and synthetic
text. ZIP byte equality is not required across platforms; the tests verify the
semantic DOCX properties instead.

The S2-T01 additions are `minimal-table-field-layout` for numbering, tabs,
breaks, a PAGE field, a 1x1 synthetic drawing, and a two-cell table; and
`minimal-header-footer-layout` for paragraph-level/final sections plus internal
header/footer references.

The S2-T02 addition is `minimal-style-inheritance-layout`. It contains only
synthetic document defaults, paragraph and character `basedOn` chains, direct
overrides, theme-font slots, explicit false/zero values, and a style-level
numbering reference. Cycle, duplicate, missing-style, type-mismatch, and depth
cases remain temporary test packages rather than permanent fixtures.

The S2-T03 addition is `minimal-numbered-heading-layout`. It covers a synthetic
multilevel numbering catalog, start override, Roman/decimal/letter labels,
numbering-linked headings, a numbered ordinary list, a skipped heading level,
and a header heading that is excluded from the main outline. Malformed and
unsupported definitions remain temporary test packages.

The S2-T04 addition is `minimal-document-sections-layout`. It covers exact
Indonesian/English abstract aliases, chapter markers, one child section,
front/main/back boundaries, references, appendices, a duplicate abstract, and
table/header/footer headings that must be excluded. Long headings, malformed
boundaries, and other ambiguity cases remain temporary test packages.

The S3-T04 golden pair is `minimal-invalid-layout` (before) and
`minimal-invalid-layout-justified` (expected after). Only the direct paragraph
alignment changes from left to justified; text and every other synthetic layout
property remain identical.

To add a fixture, first add its manifest entry and a narrow test purpose, then
extend the generator, regenerate, and add expected properties or a focused file
under `expected/`. Do not update an expected result merely to hide a parser or
fixer regression. Re-run the sanitization and immutability checks before commit.

The S5-T04 addition is `document-page-map-multipage`. It contains explicit
page and section breaks, headings, abstract/body content, mixed runs, a
hyperlink, a table, a long boundary paragraph, and identical paragraph text on
different pages. Page assertions use injected structural bookmarks and PDF
named destinations; duplicate text is never searched or matched.
